en: [0] [Success! Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas!

[1] Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagṛha, in the Cool Grove (Śītavana), in the great cemetery (mahāśmaśāna), in the vicinity of the Iṅghikāyātana. There, the Venerable Rāhula was being excessively tormented by celestial spirits (devagraha), serpent spirits (nāgagraha), yakṣa spirits (yakṣagraha), rākṣasa spirits (rākṣasagraha), kinnara spirits (kinnaragraha), garuḍa spirits (garuḍagraha), mahoraga spirits (mahoragagraha), human spirits (manuṣyagraha), non-human spirits (amanuṣyagraha), preta spirits (pretagraha), bhūta spirits (bhūtagraha), piśāca spirits (piśācagraha), and kumbhāṇḍa spirits (kumbhāṇḍagraha); as well as by leopards, crows, owls, insects, reptiles, and other beings, both human and non-human.

[2] Then the Venerable Rāhula approached the Blessed One; having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, he circumambulated the Blessed One three times and, weeping before the Blessed One, shed tears.

[3] Then the Blessed One, though already knowing, addressed Rāhula: "Rāhula, why do you stand before me shedding tears? When this was said, the Venerable Rāhula spoke thus to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, I was staying here in Rājagṛha, in the Cool Grove, in the Great Cemetery, at the site of the Iṅghikāyatana. There, Blessed One, I was harassed by celestial spirits, by nāga-spirits, by yakṣa-spirits, by rākṣasa-spirits, by kinnara-spirits, by garuḍa-spirits, by mahoraga-spirits, by human spirits, by non-human spirits, by preta-spirits, by bhūta-spirits, by piśāca-spirits, by kumbhāṇḍa-spirits, by leopards, crows, owls, insects, reptiles, and by other beings, both human and non-human."

[4] Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable Rāhula: "Rāhula, you should take up this Mahādaṇḍa dhāraṇī-vidyā. It will serve for the protection, defense, and guardianship of the fourfold assembly—of monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen—and will be for their long-term welfare, benefit, and happiness."

[5] Namely: Aṅgā, Vaṅgā, Bhaṅgā, Varaṅgā, Saṃsārataraṅgā, Sāsadaṅgā, Bhaṅgā, Jesurā, Ekatarā, Aravīrā, Taravīrā, Karavīrā, Karakaravīrā, Indrā, Indrakisarā, Haṃsā, Haṃsakisarā, Picimalā, Mahākiccā, Viheṭhikā, Kālucchikā, Aṅgodarā, Jayā, Jayālikā, Velā, Elā, Cintāli, Cili cili, Hili hili, Sumati, Vasumati, Culunaṭṭe, Culuculunnaṭṭe, Culunāḍi, Kunāḍi, Hārīṭaki, Kārīṭaki, Gauri, Gandhāri, Caṇḍāli, Mātaṅgi, Dharaṇi dhāraṇi, Uṣṭrapālike, Kacakārike, Calanāṭike, Kākalike, Lalāmati, Rakṣāmati, Varākule, Manmate, Utpale, Karavīre, Taravīre, Tarataravīre, Kuruvīre, Kurukuruvīre, Curuvīre, Curucuruvīre, Mahāvīre, Irāmati, Varāmati, Rakṣāmati, Sarvārthasādhani, Paramārthasādhani, Apratihate! King Indra; King Yama; King Varuṇa; King Kubera; King Manasvin; King Vāsuki; King Daṇḍāgni; King Brahmā, Lord of a Thousand; the Buddha, the Blessed One, the Sovereign of Dharma, the Unsurpassed One who has compassion for the world—may they grant protection, deliverance, guardianship, preservation, peace, well-being, immunity from punishment, immunity from weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth. May he live for a hundred years; may he see a hundred autumns.

[6] Namely: Balavati, Varamati, Talamati, Lakṣamati, Rakṣamati, Huru huru, Phuru phuru, Cara cara, Khara khara, Khuru khuru, Mati mati, Bhūmicaṇḍe, Kālikeṭi, Akisalā, Pīne, Sāmalate, Hūle sthūle, Sthūlaśikhare, Jaya sthūle, Jaya naṭṭe, Cala nāsi, Culu nāsi, Vāgbandhani, Virohaṇi, Solohite, Aṇḍare, Paṇḍare, Karāle, Kiṃnare, Keyūre, Ketumati, Bhūtaṃgame, Bhūtamati, Dhanye, Maṅgalye, Mahābalalohitamūle, Acaladaṇḍe, Dhuraṃdharā, Jayālike, Jayā, Gorohaṇi, Curu curu, Rundha rundha, Dhuru dhuru, Khuru khuru, Khurumati, Bandhumati, Dhuraṃdhare, Dhare dhare, Vidhare vimati, Viṣkambhaṇi, Nāśani vināśani, Bandhani, Mokṣaṇi, Mocani, Mohani, Bhāvani, Śodhani, Saṃśodhani, Viśodhani, Saṃkhiraṇi, Saṃchindani, Sādhu turumāṇe, Hara hara bandhumati, Hiri hiri, Khiri khiri, Kharali, Huru huru, Piṅgale. Homage be to the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones! Svāhā!

[7] Indeed, Rāhula, when this *Mahādaṇḍadhāraṇī* spell—having tied a knot in a sūtra of even one hundred and eight words—is worn upon the hand or worn around the neck, protection will be established for a hundred leagues in every direction. Neither humans nor non-humans shall overcome them; neither poison, nor weapons, nor disease, nor fever, nor high fever, nor spells and mantras, nor *vetāḍas* [shall prevail]. One shall not meet death by illness, fire, poison, or water. It is a binder of all applications of spells and mantras, even those well-employed, and a liberator from the bonds of others. It brings about the destruction of all diseases, sorrows, and obstacles; it pacifies the defilements of the *kali*-age; it effects liberation from all planetary seizures (*graha*). Should any seizure not release [the person], his head shall split into seven pieces like the cluster of blossoms on an *arjaka* tree. Moreover, Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the Yakṣas, having meditated with his vajra blazing, flaming, and becoming a single mass of fire, shall split his head open. And the Four Great Kings shall destroy him with an iron wheel, striking with the edge of a razor, so that he shall fall from that world of the Yakṣas and find no dwelling in the capital city of Aḍakavatī.

[8] Indeed, Rāhula, when this *Mahādaṇḍadhāraṇī* spell is recited even once, one who has fallen into the midst of kings, thieves, water, fire, poison, weapons, forests, wildernesses, mountains, or difficult passes is liberated from all fears. This *Mahādaṇḍadhāraṇī* spell has been spoken, is being spoken, and will be spoken by Buddhas as numerous as the sands of ninety-one Ganges rivers; it is perfected, supremely perfected, and is worshipped by all gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas. Amidst all fears and calamities, may there be auspiciousness and health for me and for all sentient beings!
[9] Thus spoke the Blessed One; the Venerable Rāhula, being uplifted, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.
[10] The Noble Mahādaṇḍadhāraṇī Śītavatī is completed.
